business: Clockout (Donovin Sims, Roscoe IL) — business optimization and AI implementation for owner-led local businesses
by_segment: Independent operator or solo professional (single truck, solo agent, one-chair shop)
Owner of a 2-9 person trade or home-service business (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, landscaping, cleaning, auto, restoration)
Owner of a 10-25 person service business (multi-crew trades, dental/medical office, retail, property services)
Small property manager or portfolio operator (40-200 units)
by_behaviour: Fast decider when trust is there
Burned before by a marketing agency
why_not: I decide fast when I trust the guy, and I do not know Donovin yet - an hour of my day in the middle of jobs to hear what is wrong with my setup feels like the start of a sales pitch, not a favor. And I am not letting someone AI touch the phone when a wrong answer costs me a repeat customer.

I have already paid somebody $1,500 a month for a year to tell me about clicks instead of jobs, so a free hour and a one-page write-up does not get me back in that chair. If the fix is real, tell me the fix and the price in the email and skip the meeting.

I already pay for a CRM, a scheduler and a review tool I use about a third of, so my gut says the answer is not another thing I have to manage. A free hour sounds fine, but I know how that ends, a write-up and a pitch.
I buy on referrals, and I do not know Donovin or anyone who has used him. Nothing here tells me who in town hired Clockout and whether it worked out.

Thirty-five hundred bucks is two months of what I would pay a bookkeeper, and I cannot see the number he would save me until after I have already given him an hour I do not have. Free look sounds like a sales call, and I do those from the truck or not at all.
I am not paying $1,500 to $3,500 for somebody to tell me what I already know about my own quotes. For a free hour I might listen, but my gut says it turns into a sales pitch.

It is not that it sounds wrong, it is that nothing is on fire badly enough this month to justify handing a stranger an hour and then a few grand. I already pay for software I half-use and I built the site myself, so I would probably hear you set this up wrong and get defensive.

I already know where my time goes, it is the same three places every week, so paying someone $1,500 to $3,500 to tell me what I already suspect does not add up against what that money buys me elsewhere. I set all this up myself and I would rather keep tinkering at 11pm than hand over accounts and a check.
why_yes: The free hour I would take, because he says he will tell me to change a process or use software I already pay for instead of selling me something, that is not how a guy selling a $3,000 job talks. But I am not handing money to somebody I met off a flyer until he has proven he will not leave me holding a mess.
flip: A couple of owners I know in the area telling me straight that he looked at their setup and told them to change a process instead of selling them something - one name I trust, and I would take the meeting and probably decide on the spot.

A one-page sample of what you would actually write up for a business like mine, with the price and the finish line on it, sent to my phone - no meeting first. And someone in McHenry or Winnebago County whose quote-to-job time actually dropped who will take my call.
A name, a local number, and a guy who will come stand in my shop and show me exactly what he would change before I pay a dime.
A reference from an owner in the trades around here who let him touch their phone and quoting, plus he shows me the fix first and I approve every word that goes to a customer before it goes live.

Two or three owners I know, a plumber and an electrician within an hour of Roscoe, telling me straight that he fixed a real leak in their follow-up and did not touch their accounts or upsell them. Give me their numbers and I will call them myself.
A flat number in writing up front and one of my own vendors or landlords telling me it paid for itself in the first 60 days.
Someone I actually know, a plumber or electrician around here, telling me Donovin fixed their intake and it stuck. Then I would take the free look, not before.
Proof from a business like mine, a truck or a one-chair shop, not a big company, that says plainly how many jobs they got out of it and what they paid, and that I can call that person myself.
Two owners of businesses my size, nearby, who will take my call and tell me what he actually fixed and what it cost them.

If a manager I actually know in the area used him and could name the exact thing he fixed and what it cost, I would spend the free hour. Referral from someone who is not him is the only thing that moves me.
Two owners I actually know in the trade, one of them with a shop my size, telling me he walked their quote-and-schedule mess and it stuck without breaking anything. Then I would take the free look.

Someone in my line of work, another trades or dental office owner within an hour of Roscoe, telling me he found a real number, like ten hours a week or $4k in quotes that went cold, and that Donovin stuck to the number he quoted. Referral beats a pitch.
If he looked at my setup and named the exact step costing me money in my own numbers, on that free page, and showed two other shops around here my size who paid and got it back, then maybe.

If someone I actually know in the business, another landlord, not a referral from him, told me the fix landed in writing with a number attached and he left them fully able to run it, I would take the free hour seriously.

He comes to me instead of me going to him, 20 minutes at my shop while I am between calls, and shows me one concrete fix he already did for another shop like mine, with the price printed on it before I open my books.
Two or three names of owner-led shops my size that I could actually call, and one who will say what the fix did to their booked jobs in dollars, not clicks.
A name I trust, my accountant, my equipment guy, or another owner two towns over, says they used him and it paid for itself.

If he showed me, on the free look, two or three quote follow-ups I dropped last month and what that cost me in dollars, then quoted the fix at under a thousand and took the risk of me not paying if it does not work.

Someone I actually know in the trades, a guy in Roscoe or Rockford who runs a crew I respect, telling me the free hour found a specific thing and the fix came in under two grand, with the number written down before he started.
